You are performing a fail-closed visual QA of one responsive derivative of an official museum collection image for mobile web display. Inspect the actual attached image pixels, including at mobile-scaled viewing. Asset key: 480. Determine whether the artwork's main subject and repeated double-headed bird motifs remain clearly readable, and whether there are any visible compression or scaling artifacts (blockiness, ringing, banding, severe blur, corruption, clipping introduced by processing). This is a museum image with no GPT-generated text, so OCR exact match is not applicable and must be reported as the literal string "N/A". Return concise JSON only with keys asset_key, vision_mobile_readable (boolean), artifacts (boolean), ocr_exact_match (string), observations (string). Fail closed: if you cannot truly inspect the image, set vision_mobile_readable false and explain.

480.observations: The full rectangular mantle remains identifiable at mobile scale; the dark central field, staggered rows of red double-headed bird motifs, and broad patterned border are clearly readable. Fine embroidery is naturally reduced, with no visible blockiness, ringing, banding, severe blur, corruption, or processing-induced clipping.

768.observations: The complete mantle and its visual hierarchy remain clear at mobile scale. Individual double-headed bird motifs, alternating row rhythm, dark field, dense red border, and historic losses at left remain distinguishable, with no visible compression or scaling artifacts.

1280.observations: The full textile is clearly readable when scaled for mobile; repeated double-headed birds, their alternating orientations, border compartments, weave color, fringe, and original damaged areas remain distinct. No blockiness, ringing, banding, smearing, distortion, or processing-induced clipping is visible.

fallback.observations: The JPEG fallback preserves the complete composition and clear subject identity at mobile scale. Repeated bird motifs, dark central field, patterned border, fringe, and original textile losses remain readable without visible compression or scaling artifacts.
